answer:
**A mean can lie where almost no real outcome occurs.** If a target is equally likely near -3 and +3, squared-error regression predicts near zero. That minimizes expected squared error but hides the two plausible alternatives. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

A mixture density network predicts component probabilities, means, and scales conditional on x. Softmax makes mixture weights sum to one; a positive parameterization ensures valid scales. The resulting density is the weighted sum of component densities.

**Train the density, not only its mean.** Evaluate negative log likelihood using log-sum-exp for stability. At inference, report mode-specific probabilities, sample outcomes, or derive an appropriate decision from the full distribution. Averaging the modes back to zero can discard the benefit.

Guard against components collapsing to tiny variance around individual observations, unused components, and interchangeable component labels. More components increase flexibility but require more evidence. Check held-out likelihood and predictive calibration, including tails. A multimodal model is justified when the conditional outcomes really need it, not simply because a more complicated density can fit training data better.

**Technical details and references.**

A mixture density network predicts weights $\pi_k(x)$, means $\mu_k(x)$, and positive scales $\sigma_k(x)$, giving $p(y|x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\pi_k\mathcal N(y;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)$. Use softmax weights, positive scale parameterization, and log-sum-exp to minimize negative log likelihood stably. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

If two outcomes near -3 and +3 are plausible, an MSE regressor predicts their mean near zero, which may itself be implausible. A mixture can retain both modes; sample from it or report mode-specific probabilities and intervals. Guard against variance collapse, unused components, and label switching. More components increase flexibility but also estimation difficulty. Evaluate held-out likelihood and predictive calibration rather than only error of the mixture mean.
